outcome: labor induction success (normal vaginal delivery vs. cesarean section)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 55 patients undergoing labor induction (46 resulting in normal vaginal delivery and 9 in cesarean section).
finding: The anterior cervical angle (ACA) was significantly different between normal vaginal delivery and cesarean section groups, with an optimal threshold of 96 degrees for predicting failure of progression, although its independent predictive value for induction success was limited compared to factors like primiparity and BMI.
mod_finding: The anterior cervical angle was significantly different between normal vaginal delivery (108.02 ± 22.38deg) and cesarean section (86.11 ± 26.09deg) groups.
